properties.natural_language: Before generating initial Whisk k values for validators at fork activation, the system must verify that get_initial_whisk_k() produces deterministic, cryptographically secure values that cannot be predicted or influenced by external attackers.
The EIP7441_FORK_EPOCH must always be a multiple of RUN_DURATION_IN_EPOCHS to ensure proper Whisk shuffling alignment, otherwise the chain must halt or reject activation.
After executing upgrade_to_eip7441, all validators must have valid k-commitments and trackers stored in the beacon state, with no validators missing cryptographic material.
The three post-upgrade selection operations (retroactive candidate, proposer, current candidate) must complete atomically without interruption to ensure Whisk is fully operational.
The saturating_sub(epoch, PROPOSER_SELECTION_GAP + 1) offset for retroactive candidate selection must prevent seed collision with proposer selection to maintain anonymity guarantees.

Before accepting any gossip message from EDGE-PEER-SENDS-GOSSIP, the node must decompress and verify the payload is <= 10 MiB, compute message ID with appropriate domain prefix, and reject oversized messages with peer scoring penalty.

When EDGE-NEW-PEER establishes a connection, the mandatory Status exchange must compare fork digests and immediately disconnect peers with mismatched fork digests to prevent cross-chain message propagation.

Messages arriving via EDGE-CLOCK-CHECK must have timestamps within MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY (500ms) tolerance, with future messages beyond this window IGNORED (not REJECTED) to avoid penalizing peers with slight clock drift.
For oversized messages detected via EDGE-OVERSIZED-DROP, the snappy decompression library must enforce the 10 MiB size limit before full decompression to prevent memory exhaustion attacks.

After validating a beacon block via gossip, the result must be exactly one of ACCEPT (forward to mesh), REJECT (penalize sender), or IGNORE (silent discard), with REJECT outcomes triggering peer score updates.
Peer scores must be continuously updated based on message validation outcomes, with peers below score threshold disconnected to prevent Sybil domination of the GossipSub mesh (target D=8).

After requesting blocks via BeaconBlocksByRange or BeaconBlocksByRoot, response chunks must be validated with single-byte result codes (0=success, 1=invalid, 2=server error, 3=unavailable) and rate limiting applied between chunks.

Nodes must maintain at least 2 persistent subnet subscriptions computed deterministically from node ID, valid for EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION (256 epochs), to ensure adequate mesh coverage and attestation propagation.

Before processing block headers from EDGE-RECEIVE-HEADER, the difficulty value must be independently computed from parent header and bomb delay offset (9,000,000 blocks), with mismatches causing immediate block rejection.
When reading block number via EDGE-READ-BLOCK-NUM for difficulty calculation, integer underflow must be prevented via max(0, block_number - 9,000,000) clamping to ensure safe bomb delay computation.

After computing the difficulty bomb component, the exponential calculation 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2) must produce non-negative values and be combined with base difficulty for final block difficulty.
After executing block transactions and applying rewards, the computed state root must match the header's state_root value, with mismatches causing block rejection.
All network participants must implement identical difficulty adjustment algorithms including the 9,000,000 block bomb delay, otherwise difficulty mismatches will cause chain splits.
Parent block timestamps used in difficulty calculations must be within reasonable bounds (typically 900 seconds tolerance) to prevent timestamp manipulation attacks affecting network difficulty.

When receiving blocks via EDGE-PEER-SENDS-BLOCK, the system must check the block number against the Byzantium activation threshold (4,370,000 mainnet) and apply the correct validation ruleset atomically for all 9 component EIPs.
When Byzantium activates at the fork block, all 9 component EIPs (100, 140, 196, 197, 198, 211, 214, 649, 658) must enable atomically without partial activation or ordering dependencies.
Blocks with block_number < fork_threshold must be validated with pre-Byzantium rules, while blocks >= fork_threshold must use Byzantium rules, with non-upgraded peers forking off the main chain.
At node startup, the system must load network-specific fork configuration (mainnet: 4,370,000, Ropsten: 1,700,000) and cache the fork block number before processing any blocks.
Block numbers must be monotonically increasing and cannot be manipulated by miners, as this would allow attackers to avoid fork activation or selectively apply old vs new validation rules.

EIP submissions from external authors must pass comprehensive validation including RFC 822 preamble format, title/description length constraints, required sections, ISO 8601 date formats, and anchored external links before editor assignment.
All EIPs must have a Security Considerations section with adequate threat modeling, attack vectors, and mitigations; missing or inadequate security treatment must block progression to Final status.
Core EIPs must be discussed on AllCoreDevs calls with cross-client implementation assessment to reach rough consensus (no sustained objections) before progressing to Final status.
After Last Call period completion without normative changes, the EIP may transition to Final; if normative changes are required, it must return to Review status before re-entering Last Call.
EIPs in Draft, Review, or Last Call status with no activity for 6+ months must be automatically marked Stagnant, but can be resurrected by author or editor via PR submission.

External links in EIPs must be anchored to specific commits to prevent post-finalization content modification; EIP editors must be trusted to make impartial decisions without gatekeeping legitimate proposals.
Core EIPs affecting consensus must include mandatory test cases before finalization, while all EIPs require a CC0 copyright waiver to ensure public domain dedication.
Before allowing an account to exist in state, the account MUST have at least one non-empty property (code, nonce > 0, or balance > 0) in post-merge state
Post-merge state MUST NEVER contain empty accounts (accounts where code is empty AND nonce equals 0 AND balance equals 0)
For networks identified as Ethereum mainnet (merge block hash equals 0x56a9bb0302da44b8c0b3df540781424684c3af04d0b7a38d72842b762076a664), the absence of empty accounts is guaranteed
After clearing empty accounts pre-merge, the state transitioning to merge MUST be verified to contain zero empty accounts
Any operation that would result in an account with code=empty AND nonce=0 AND balance=0 post-merge MUST enter undefined behavior state and be rejected
For non-mainnet networks to guarantee no empty accounts, the network MUST have had no empty accounts at genesis AND Spurious Dragon fork active from block 0
Before executing a LOG opcode, the EVM MUST verify the execution is NOT in a static call context to prevent state modification violations
After successfully executing a LOG instruction, the log entry MUST contain the executing contract's actual address, not a spoofed or manipulated address
After reading log data from memory, if memory expansion is required, the expansion cost MUST be charged before the log is emitted, or the operation MUST revert with out-of-gas
LOG operations MUST be atomic: either the complete log entry is recorded in the logs list OR the operation reverts entirely with no partial state
Before charging gas for a LOG instruction, all gas components MUST be calculated: base LOG gas, data gas (GAS_LOG_DATA * size), topic gas (GAS_LOG_TOPIC * num_topics), and memory expansion gas
If a LOG instruction execution fails at any gas charging step (base, data, topic, or memory), the EVM MUST enter out-of-gas state and revert without emitting the log
After popping topic values from the stack, topics MUST be converted to 32-byte big-endian format using to_be_bytes32() before inclusion in the log entry
Before storing an inclusion list, the system MUST verify the list was received before the view freeze deadline for the target slot, or reject it as late
Before accepting an inclusion list from a validator, the system MUST check if the validator has already submitted a different inclusion list for the same (Slot, Root) pair to detect equivocation
After detecting equivocation from a validator, ALL inclusion lists from that validator for the slot MUST be excluded from get_inclusion_list_transactions aggregation
After retrieving inclusion list transactions for a slot, the returned set MUST contain only deduplicated transactions from valid, non-equivocating, timely inclusion lists

The InclusionListStore MUST maintain the invariant that if a validator index is in the equivocators mapping for a slot, none of that validator's inclusion lists for that slot contribute to get_inclusion_list_transactions
Before processing an inclusion list submission, the validator identity MUST be authenticated to ensure the validator index in the equivocation check corresponds to the actual submitter
Before processing a wallet_watchAsset request, the wallet MUST validate the asset type is recognized (e.g., ERC20, ERC1046) and reject unrecognized types
Before accepting a wallet_watchAsset request, the token contract address MUST be validated as 0x-prefixed checksummed hexadecimal and checksum verification MUST pass
Before fetching token image metadata, the image URL MUST use a whitelisted scheme (https, ipfs, data) and MUST NOT target localhost or internal network addresses (SSRF protection)
After validating a wallet_watchAsset request, the wallet MUST return the response (true or error) to the dApp BEFORE showing any user interaction prompt to prevent fingerprinting
After detecting a token with similar name/symbol to a known token but different address or chain, the wallet MUST display a phishing warning to the user before the approval prompt
The wallet MUST treat all data from dApp wallet_watchAsset requests as untrusted and perform full validation regardless of the dApp's origin
Before processing a wallet_watchAsset request, if a chain ID is specified, the wallet MUST verify it recognizes the chain ID or reject the request for unknown chains
Before deserializing untrusted SSZ bytes, the deserializer MUST validate that all offsets are strictly increasing, within bounds, and properly aligned to minimum element sizes
Before deserializing a list from SSZ bytes, the deserializer MUST verify the deserialized list length does not exceed the declared maximum capacity N
Before deserializing a union type from SSZ bytes, the selector byte MUST be validated to be in the range 0-127 and correspond to a defined type variant
After deserializing SSZ bytes, the deserializer MUST verify there are no excess trailing bytes; all input bytes must be consumed or the data is malformed
After deserializing a bitlist, the deserializer MUST verify the sentinel bit is present and correctly positioned to determine the bitlist length
SSZ serialization MUST be deterministic: serializing the same typed object multiple times MUST produce bit-identical output across all implementations
Merkleization MUST produce collision-resistant hash tree roots: distinct SSZ objects MUST yield distinct 32-byte hash tree roots
After computing a hash tree root for a variable-length type (list or bitlist), the merkle root MUST be mixed with the serialized uint256 length to produce the final hash tree root
Before deserializing SSZ data from an untrusted source, implementations SHOULD enforce a maximum nesting depth to prevent stack overflow during recursive deserialization
All SSZ deserialization failures MUST result in rejection of the data without crashes or undefined behavior; malformed data MUST NOT cause implementation-specific vulnerabilities
